source_notes.label: Bulky carboxylate and dynamic amine roles
source_notes.summary: The authors propose that bulky adamantanecarboxylate provides steric stabilization while more dynamic HDA binding supports a soluble colloid. ACA-only particles are crystalline but polydisperse and poorly soluble; HDA or dodecylamine restores a clear colloid, whereas extra ACA does not. This is a source interpretation, not a measured ligand coverage or unique conformation.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3–4, Ligand comparisons and proposed stabilization

source_notes.label: Injection temperature versus heating time
source_notes.summary: Higher injection temperature gives smaller, more uniform particles in the reported HDA/DPE and TDPA/DPE families. The authors discuss nucleation and growth separation. Heating for 1 min, 40 min or 3 h changes nanowire abundance more strongly than the spherical-particle sizes; missing table continuation cells remain explicitly inherited.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–3, Table 1 and temperature/time discussion

source_notes.label: Seed enlargement has a finite useful range
source_notes.summary: One additional precursor injection increases a reported 4.0 nm seed population to 6.2 nm. More than two added injections gives about 10 nm irregular, polydisperse polycrystalline particles. The main SI declaration names three additions, but the SI itself is unreviewed. The 7.2 nm diffraction inset label is not assigned to an invented two-addition recipe.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–4, 6, Additional injections and SI declaration

source_notes.label: Alloy assignment and the remaining alternative
source_notes.summary: ICP-AES and EDX report an approximately 1:3 Co/Pt ratio across the preparations. XRD and HRTEM support chemically disordered fcc CoPt3. The authors explicitly note that diffraction alone cannot completely exclude phase segregation or a core–shell model, then argue against those alternatives using TEM contrast and composition behavior. No measured atomic coordinates, ordered L12 cell or core–shell interface is asserted.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 4, Structural characterization; Figure 2

source_notes.label: Particle packing is not atomic crystal structure
source_notes.summary: Figure 3 depicts layer-by-layer particle assemblies with ccp-like packing. Figure 4 depicts AB5/CaCu5-type packing formed from 4.5 and 2.6 nm CoPt3 particles. Both particle species are CoPt3; CaCu5 is a packing analogy, not another chemical phase or material made here.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 5, Figures 3–4 and assembly discussion

source_notes.label: Interparticle spacing and shell language remain qualified
source_notes.summary: The source first describes about 2.5 nm interparticle spacing and later uses about 2.5 nm organic-shell wording. These descriptions are retained in parallel; they are not converted into a unique radial shell thickness, molecular length or interfacial coordinate model.

source_notes.label: Controlled oversaturation builds whole colloidal crystals
source_notes.summary: A toluene nanocrystal dispersion is layered with 2-propanol and methanol. After about 2–3 weeks the source obtains facetted 10–20 µm colloidal crystals. Those dimensions describe whole assemblies, not the constituent nanocrystal diameter; the exact building-block size is unassigned.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2, 6, Preparation of Colloidal Crystals; Figure 5 and Summary

source_notes.label: Thermal stability depends on atmosphere
source_notes.summary: Air annealing at 100 or 200 °C for 2 h retains solubility and shows no oxide by XRD. At 300 °C the sample becomes insoluble, with weak reflections tentatively assigned to CoO and a main peak shift toward Pt-rich alloy. Vacuum treatments at 400 and 500 °C show no crystalline oxide; their duration is not independently stated. CoO/Co3O4 reference sticks are not two observed oxide products.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 6, Thermostability and Figure 6

source_notes.label: Post-workup ligand addition is a stability treatment
source_notes.summary: Washed colloids can leave a film after several days. About 0.1 mg HDA per 25 mg nanocrystals dissolves it promptly, and the colloid then remains stable in air for months. This qualitative storage context is distinct from growth and does not create another measured particle-size outcome.
